solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fish pie and odd bits from chef — something extra for the man?

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first and third, are taken from the word chef

explanation.surface: A cook's fish pie with scraps of garnish, plus a little bonus for the gentleman diner.
explanation.walkthrough: COD and PIE are joined, then C and E, the odd letters of 'chef'.
explanation.definitionFit: A codpiece was a pouch added to the front of men's breeches in Tudor dress, a jokey extra item of male clothing.

clue.text: Concerns excluding first of electric vehicles

indicators.note: excluding says a letter is left out of the word for concerns
first of picks the opening letter of the word electric

explanation.surface: Worries about electric cars, minus the first one built.
explanation.definitionFit: Cars are motor vehicles, the plural noun matching the plural definition.

clue.text: Haul part of hospital up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for the hospital section is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a ward is a section of a hospital

explanation.surface: Dragging a piece of a hospital up the stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw is to pull or drag, as a horse draws a cart, the same as to haul.

clue.text: In this state one won't have got ready

definitions.text: In this state one won't have got ready

parts.words: In this state one won't have got ready
parts.note: ready is slang for cash (ready money), so the state is one of having no money to pay debts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Got ready' reads like being prepared; 'the ready' is old slang for cash, so this is the state of having none.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolvency is the condition of being unable to pay one's debts, of lacking funds.

clue.text: Scoundrel to stop supply of tea

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
to die is to stop, as an engine dies

explanation.surface: A villain trying to cut off someone's tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Caddie is an accepted variant spelling of caddy, a box for storing tea; the clue may also hint at a golf caddie handing over tees.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy, also spelt caddie, is the container in which a household keeps its stock of tea leaves.

clue.text: Observe daughter or other offspring

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: Watch your daughter or your other children.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed is an old word for descendants or progeny, as in biblical 'the seed of Abraham'.

clue.text: Total runs one piled up including nothing on a big scale

indicators.note: including means the letter for nothing is placed inside
in a down clue, piled up means the stacked pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batsman's total of runs piling up from nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: SUM, R and ONE read upwards give ENORMUS; 'including' then puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous means huge, so something done on a big scale is enormous in size.

clue.text: Unease I'd picked up: I should participate in new quest

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the letters of I'd are lifted and read upwards

parts.note: taken as I and D, the contraction of I had or I would

indicators.note: the I should take part in, so it is put inside the rearranged quest
new means the letters of quest are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone uneasy at what they've learned, insisting on joining a new quest.
explanation.walkthrough: ID upwards gives DI; QUEST rearranged as SQUET takes I inside, making SQUIET.
explanation.definitionFit: Disquiet is a feeling of anxiety or worry, a close synonym of unease.

clue.text: Where are the billboards? Zero adverts seen during journey

indicators.note: seen during means these letters appear in the middle of the word for journey

explanation.surface: No advertising visible on the trip, though where are the hoardings?
explanation.definitionFit: Billboards are typically placed along the edge of the road where passing drivers can read them.

clue.text: Sensible attitude excluding America?

parts.note: no, as in 'no US', means without or excluding
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A sly dig that a sensible outlook means leaving America out.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is British slang, from Greek, for common sense or practical intelligence.

clue.text: Source of decoration using cigar in an unusual way

indicators.note: the letters are put together in an unusual way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Decorating something by using a cigar oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing sugar is the fine powdered sugar used to make the icing that decorates cakes.

clue.text: Welsh party MP daily excited about start of Cardiff rugby

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
excited means the letters of MP and daily are stirred up and rearranged
start of takes the opening letter of the city's name

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A Welsh politician gets excited by a newspaper report about a Cardiff rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: MP DAILY rearranged gives PLAIDYM, around C, then RU follows. Cardiff is the Welsh capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid Cymru is the Welsh nationalist political party; its name is Welsh for 'Party of Wales'.

clue.text: Sword? I'm the very thing involved in evidence of wound

indicators.note: involved in means the pieces are set inside the word for a wound's mark

parts.note: a scar is the mark left by a wound
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
it means the very thing, as in 'that's it!'

explanation.surface: A sword boasting that it is just the thing to leave a wound's trace.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved single-edged sabre of Middle Eastern origin.

clue.text: Partisan reviewed prospective member?

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the word is looked over again and its letters reworked

explanation.surface: A biased supporter reconsidered as a possible recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone hoping to achieve a position, such as a would-be member of a club or party.

clue.text: Money we kept back to get nut

indicators.note: kept back means the word we is held in reverse order

explanation.surface: We held back some money to buy nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is a kidney-shaped edible nut from a tropical tree.

clue.text: Tolerate final treatment after head's cut

parts.note: the end is the final part

indicators.note: after its head is cut, the word for treatment loses its first letter

parts.note: a cure is a medical treatment

explanation.surface: Putting up with a last round of treatment after a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to bear or put up with something unpleasant, a synonym of tolerate.

clue.text: Like a nuanced view? It's not evident in words on screen

indicators.note: not evident in means those letters are missing from the on-screen words

parts.note: a subtitle is text shown on screen
read as 'IT is', so the letters IT

explanation.surface: A nuanced point is lost in the subtitles of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'It's not evident in' as 'IT is absent from': SUBTITLE without IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtle view is delicate and finely distinguished, which is what nuanced describes.

clue.text: Something that's served up route taken at sea?

parts.note: the main is a literary word for the open sea
a course is a route or path

explanation.surface: A dish brought out, or a ship's heading at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Route taken at sea' reads as COURSE on the MAIN, the main being the high seas.
explanation.definitionFit: The main course is the principal dish of a meal, served after the starter.

clue.text: Stop offering no initial comfort

indicators.note: offering no initial means the word for stop loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Ending something without giving the first bit of reassurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is relief from pain or worry, the state of comfort.

clue.text: Close — initially not even remote? Not initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the next two words
not initially means the word for remote is used without its first letter

explanation.surface: Close, or perhaps not even remote at first: a speaker hedging about distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Near means close by in space or time, a direct synonym of close as an adjective.

clue.text: Starts to take hold after winter? This may

definitions.text: Starts to take hold after winter? This may

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letter of each of the following four words

explanation.surface: Something that starts to take hold when winter ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A thaw, the melting of ice and snow, sets in as winter ends and warmer weather arrives.

clue.text: Nag, distressed, in perturbed condition, to stop moving

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the word for a perturbed condition

parts.note: to be in a state is to be agitated or upset

indicators.note: distressed means the word nag is disturbed and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: An upset horse in a bad way stops in its tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: NAG jumbled as GNA goes inside STATE; 'in a state' is British for agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stop flowing or developing, like still water going stale.

clue.text: Radio's correct form of liturgy

indicators.note: what the radio broadcasts is heard, not seen, so the word is taken by its sound

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's approved version of a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a prescribed ceremonial act, as in a religious service.

clue.text: Try and try to produce supportive comment

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court
again, to hear as a judge does

explanation.surface: Keep trying to say something encouraging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is in the legal sense: a judge tries, or hears, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Hear hear' is the cry of agreement used in Parliament and at meetings to back a speaker.
